blocks.content: PART A: CONCEPT OF PUBLIC FINANCE

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Public finance covers public revenue, expenditure, government budget, deficits, and public debt.
Taxes are classified into direct and indirect taxes, as well as progressive, proportional, and regressive structures.
Government expenditure is categorized into revenue vs capital and developmental vs non-developmental types.
Fiscal Deficit represents the total net borrowing requirement of the government for the fiscal year.
Primary Deficit isolates the current year's fiscal imbalance by subtracting interest payments on past loans from the Fiscal Deficit.

blocks.content: 1. Meaning of Public Finance

Public finance is the branch of economics that studies the financial activities of the government. It explains how the government collects money (revenue), how it spends money (expenditure), how it borrows money (public debt), and how these activities affect the economy.
Unlike private finance, public finance focuses on social welfare and public interest, not profit.
PART B: PUBLIC REVENUE – DEEP EXPLANATION
2. Public Revenue
Public revenue refers to all income received by the government to meet its administrative, developmental and welfare expenditure.
3. Taxes – Concept + Logic
Taxes are compulsory contributions imposed by the government on individuals and businesses without any direct return. Taxes are the main source of public revenue.
4. Types of Taxes (Detailed)

Direct Taxes are imposed directly on income and wealth. Example: Income Tax.



Indirect Taxes are imposed on goods and services and are collected indirectly. Example: GST.
5. Progressive, Proportional & Regressive Tax – WITH GRAPH LOGIC

Progressive Tax:

In progressive taxation, tax rate increases as income increases. Graphically, income is shown on X-axis and tax paid on Y-axis. The curve becomes steeper as income increases.



Proportional Tax:

Tax rate remains constant at all income levels. The graph is a straight line rising uniformly.



Regressive Tax:

Tax rate decreases as income increases. The curve rises but at a decreasing rate.
PART C: PUBLIC EXPENDITURE – WITH CONCEPTUAL GRAPH
6. Public Expenditure
Public expenditure refers to spending by the government on administration, defence, education, health, infrastructure and welfare programmes.
7. Types of Public Expenditure (Explained)

Revenue Expenditure includes day-to-day expenses such as salaries and subsidies.



Capital Expenditure includes long-term investment like roads, dams and railways.
8. Growth of Public Expenditure – GRAPH EXPLANATION
Graphically, public expenditure is shown increasing over time. On X-axis time is taken, on Y-axis government expenditure. The upward-sloping curve shows increasing role of government.
PART D: GOVERNMENT BUDGET – COMPLETE LOGIC

rows: Indicates government shortfall in meeting daily operational expenses.
Measures total financial borrowings required by the government.
Shows borrowing requirements purely for current year spending.

blocks.content: 9. Budget
A government budget is an annual statement showing estimated receipts and expenditures for a financial year.
10. Objectives of Budget – WITH FLOW LOGIC

Allocation of resources ensures efficient use of resources.

Redistribution reduces inequality.

Economic stability controls inflation and deflation.

Growth promotes development.
PART E: DEFICITS – MOST IMPORTANT WITH GRAPHS
11. Revenue Deficit – GRAPH EXPLANATION
Revenue deficit occurs when revenue expenditure exceeds revenue receipts. Graphically, revenue expenditure line lies above revenue receipts line.
12. Fiscal Deficit – GRAPH EXPLANATION
Fiscal deficit represents total borrowing requirement. Graph shows total expenditure above total receipts excluding borrowings.

items: Formula Alert: Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Net Interest Payments.
Fiscal Deficit equals total government borrowings and liabilities incurred in a financial year.
Difference between Progressive Tax (rate increases with income) and Regressive Tax (effective rate decreases as income increases).

blocks.content: 13. Primary Deficit – LOGIC
Primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments. It shows current fiscal position excluding past debt burden.
PART F: PUBLIC DEBT – FULL EXPLANATION
14. Public Debt
Public debt refers to government borrowings to finance deficits. Internal debt is borrowed within country; external debt is borrowed from foreign sources.
SSC ULTRA FINAL REVISION POINTS

• Public finance = government income & spending

• Taxes are main revenue source

• Progressive tax reduces inequality

• Budget is annual financial plan

• Fiscal deficit shows borrowing need
